title: When Lester Young left the band and Don Byas replaced him
summary: They sort out the early 1940s, with Lester leaving for a USO tour with Al Sears and Don Byas taking his place.

story.theme_name: Drafted: musicians in the military and the war years
story.community_name: Drafted: service bands, USO shows and the war years

blocks.x: I see, that's most interesting. Now, you went in the service so it was usually a routine thing all through the 40's until 1944, I guess. Can you think of anything that happened between that and 1944 when you went in the Army? What were the complete happenings in the band? From '39 to when you went in the Army.
All right. Lester — we were doing a recording date at Columbia and I believe it was a 13th on a Friday.
What year is this now? From '39 to '44 we want to clear up what you did.
I went in the army about '44.
Lester was there up to..... Lester left the band around about 42-ish or 43-ish, because he, Al Sears, they went out - remember the war had come along.
Let's get a little more coherent now. When Lester left did Al Sears take his place?
No, they went out on the USO tour; they was playing Army camps. Lester had left the band.
Lester had left the band in '42?
We got Don Byas to play.
Lester left the band and Don Byas came in.
'42, yes, around about 42-ish, because Don made that memorial thing, 'Harvard Blues.' We did that at the Leiderkranz Hall.
Buck was there, he could have been.
And Don Byas took his place, huh?
Yes - wait a minute. You see, Don - wait a minute - this is '40 because we were at Cafe Society Uptown and Lester had left the band. He stayed out of the band for about 2 1/2 years.

He went out with Al Sears and Marlowe. I don't know whether it was Nile Morris. They had a thing going, they had a terrific band... We didn't know what they were doing because we had to take care of our things and it became hectic after '41, you know.
